summary: Metroid entries from Sami's spine and sourced supplemental seeds, built for per-platform route research.

entries.title: Metroid Dread
entries.definitive_edition: Metroid Dread Ver. 2.1.0 with free update modes

emulation.notes: Official Switch native route; no emulator required.

primary.version: Metroid Dread Ver. 2.1.0 with free update modes
primary.why: Metroid Dread is Switch-only, and the final free updates added Rookie Mode, Dread Mode, Boss Rush, Survival Rush, Dread Rush, Practice, and result-screen additions.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Switch release with the latest update installed; use the physical or digital version and confirm Ver. 2.1.0 or newer on the title screen.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or expanded edition is documented beyond the free updates.

entries.title: Metroid Fusion
entries.definitive_edition: Game Boy Advance - Nintendo Classics release

emulation.notes: Official Switch GBA Classics route; no emulator required.

primary.version: Game Boy Advance - Nintendo Classics release
primary.why: Fusion is available through the current Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack GBA Classics library, superseding older GBA cartridge, 3DS Ambassador, and Wii U Virtual Console routes for official access.
primary.how_to_play: Play through Game Boy Advance - Nintendo Classics on Nintendo Switch with Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack.

entries.remaster_caveats: Requires Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack; no remake exists.

entries.title: Metroid Other M

emulation.notes: Original Wii hardware with a Wii Remote is the reference route; emulation must preserve pointer/orientation controls.

primary.why: Other M is a Wii-only game designed around the Wii Remote orientation-switch control scheme, so the original Wii release is the complete and most faithful route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Wii disc on Wii or Wii U backward compatibility with a Wii Remote; use Dolphin only as a preservation fallback after mapping the required pointer/orientation controls.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or current official re-release exists.

entries.title: Metroid Prime 2 Echoes
entries.definitive_edition: Metroid Prime: Trilogy / New Play Control version

emulation.notes: Original Wii hardware is the official primary; Dolphin/PrimeHack-style setups are preservation/high-resolution fallbacks if controls are mapped well.

primary.version: Metroid Prime: Trilogy / New Play Control version
primary.why: The Trilogy/New Play Control version updates Echoes with Wii Remote aiming, 16:9 widescreen support, shorter loads, updated textures/bloom lighting, and lowered some difficult boss encounters while preserving Echoes multiplayer.
primary.how_to_play: Play Metroid Prime: Trilogy on Wii hardware with Wii Remote and Nunchuk, or use an already-owned Wii U eShop copy as a legacy fallback.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Trilogy package is out of print physically and the Wii U eShop is closed; use an owned copy.

entries.title: Metroid Prime 3 Corruption

emulation.notes: Original Wii hardware is the official primary; emulation must preserve Wii Remote pointer controls.

primary.why: Prime 3 was built for Wii pointer controls, and the Trilogy package keeps that design while placing it in the unified three-game collection with its extras interface.
primary.how_to_play: Play Metroid Prime: Trilogy on Wii hardware with Wii Remote and Nunchuk, or use the original Wii disc if Trilogy is unavailable.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Trilogy package is out of print physically and the Wii U eShop is closed; use an owned copy.

entries.title: Metroid Prime Federation Force

emulation.notes: Original 3DS hardware is the primary route; no emulator required.

primary.why: Federation Force is a 3DS-only game. It was designed around cooperative missions, but Nintendo 3DS online services ended in 2024, so the current complete route depends on offline/local play or historical online access.
primary.how_to_play: Play the 3DS cartridge or an already-owned digital copy; use local multiplayer where possible and treat official online matchmaking as unavailable.

entries.remaster_caveats: New eShop purchases are closed and official Nintendo 3DS online services ended April 8, 2024.

entries.title: Metroid Prime Hunters

emulation.notes: Original DS hardware is preferred for touch aiming; DS emulation is a preservation fallback.

primary.why: Hunters was designed for DS touch-screen aiming and local/online multiplayer; the Wii U Virtual Console re-release is a legacy owned-copy option, while original DS online services ended in 2014.
primary.how_to_play: Play the DS cartridge on DS-compatible hardware for the intended dual-screen/touch setup; use local multiplayer where possible and treat official online play as unavailable.

entries.remaster_caveats: Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection online play ended May 20, 2014; Wii U eShop purchases are closed.

entries.title: Metroid Prime Pinball
entries.definitive_edition: Original Nintendo DS release with optional DS Rumble Pak

emulation.notes: Original DS hardware is preferred, especially for Rumble Pak support; emulation is a preservation fallback.

primary.version: Original Nintendo DS release with optional DS Rumble Pak
primary.why: Prime Pinball is a DS-only pinball entry, originally sold with DS Rumble Pak support, so the original cartridge route is the complete primary.
primary.how_to_play: Play the DS cartridge on DS-compatible hardware; use a DS Rumble Pak if you want the intended force-feedback accessory support.

entries.title: Metroid Prime Remastered

emulation.notes: Official Switch native route; no emulator required.

primary.why: This entry is the Switch remaster, using remastered visuals, audio, controls, multiple difficulty options, and bonus galleries.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Nintendo Switch release with the latest update; choose modern dual-analog controls or a classic/Trilogy-inspired control preset based on preference.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a remaster of Metroid Prime, not Prime 2 or Prime 3.

entries.title: Metroid Samus Returns

emulation.notes: Original 3DS hardware is the primary route; no emulator required.

primary.why: Samus Returns is a 3DS-only remake of Metroid II with its own mechanics and presentation, so the original 3DS release is the complete route for this distinct game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Nintendo 3DS cartridge, or an already-owned digital copy; new 3DS eShop purchases are closed.

entries.remaster_caveats: New 3DS eShop purchases are closed; this is a remake of Metroid II, not the Game Boy original.

entries.title: Metroid Zero Mission
entries.definitive_edition: Game Boy Advance - Nintendo Classics release

emulation.notes: Official Switch GBA Classics route; no emulator required.

primary.version: Game Boy Advance - Nintendo Classics release
primary.why: Zero Mission is available through the current Switch GBA Classics library, superseding the GBA cartridge and closed Wii U Virtual Console routes for official access.
primary.how_to_play: Play through Game Boy Advance - Nintendo Classics on Nintendo Switch with Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack.

entries.remaster_caveats: Requires Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack; this is a remake of the original Metroid and should not be merged with the NES game entry.

entries.title: Super Metroid
entries.definitive_edition: Super Nintendo Entertainment System - Nintendo Classics release

emulation.notes: Official Switch SNES Classics route; no emulator required.

primary.version: Super Nintendo Entertainment System - Nintendo Classics release
primary.why: Super Metroid is included in the current Switch SNES Classics library, making it the current official route for the original SNES game with save/rewind service features.
primary.how_to_play: Play through Super Nintendo Entertainment System - Nintendo Classics with Nintendo Switch Online; use the SNES controller accessory if you want closer original-feel controls.

entries.remaster_caveats: Requires Nintendo Switch Online; no remake exists.

entries.title: Metroid
entries.definitive_edition: NES version through Nintendo Switch Online/Nintendo Classics for original-game route

emulation.emulator: Mesen / FCEUX only if official route is unavailable
emulation.notes: Use official Nintendo Classics route where possible; document emulator/core if used.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Famicom Disk System or NES hardware, depending on target region

primary.version: NES version through Nintendo Switch Online
primary.why: The 1986 original Metroid is distinct from Metroid: Zero Mission, which is already archived as a remake. The current official NES Classics route is the practical main route for the original game, while Famicom Disk System and NES hardware differences should be noted if exact-history comparison matters.
primary.how_to_play: Use the NES version through Nintendo Switch Online/Nintendo Classics. Record service version, region, controller, save-state/rewind use, password/save handling, and whether Famicom Disk System or Zero Mission was compared.

secondary.what_to_play: Compare only if exact original-region behavior matters.
secondary.why: The international NES/password route is not identical to the original FDS context.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not merge Metroid: Zero Mission into this entry; record save-state/rewind and region behavior.

entries.title: Metroid II: Return of Samus
entries.definitive_edition: Game Boy version through Nintendo Switch Online / Nintendo Classics

emulation.emulator: Nintendo Classics wrapper; SameBoy or mGBA only if official route is unavailable
emulation.notes: Use official Nintendo Classics route where possible; document emulator/core if used.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Game Boy hardware for display/control authenticity; Nintendo Classics for current access

primary.platform: Nintendo Switch / Nintendo Classics Game Boy
primary.version: Game Boy version through Nintendo Switch Online
primary.why: Metroid II is the original Game Boy sequel and is distinct from the 3DS remake Metroid: Samus Returns. The current official practical route is Nintendo's Game Boy Classics app, while original Game Boy hardware is the monochrome timing/display reference.
primary.how_to_play: Use Game Boy - Nintendo Classics on Switch. Record service/app version, region, screen style, suspend/rewind use, controller, Metroid count/progress, save state, and whether Samus Returns or AM2R was excluded.

secondary.what_to_play: Use for original-display and timing comparison.
secondary.why: Nintendo Classics is current and practical, but the Game Boy is the authenticity ceiling.

secondary.what_to_play: Archive separately or only as labeled comparison.
secondary.why: They are remakes, not replacements for the 1991 Game Boy game.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not merge with Metroid: Samus Returns or AM2R; record screen style, rewind, and save-state use.
